nodes.label: Zero External LLM API Key Constraint
nodes.rationale: The whole repo runs with no external LLM API key: the invoking coding agent (Claude Code or Pi / el Gentleman) does the reasoning itself, never a Python call to Gemini/OpenAI. This keeps Python deterministic, local and auditable, and is why there is no call_llm() anywhere in the pipeline.

nodes.label: Two-Verb Agent-Native CLI Pattern
nodes.rationale: Each LLM role follows the same shape: a deterministic two-verb CLI (`python -m chec_local_interpreter.agent_tools.<role> build-context` / `validate`) builds the context/prompt and validates the response's shape, while the invoking coding agent authors the JSON response itself. Determinism stays in Python; only interpretation is delegated.

nodes.label: Prohibited Stack in src/chec_local_interpreter
nodes.rationale: Databricks, Dash, FastAPI, RAG and vector stores must never enter src/chec_local_interpreter or any of the 5 LLM agent roles. Predictive-model inference and forecasting language are also prohibited in historical's base explanations, EXCEPT inside outputs validated by validar_respuesta_inferencia, where predictive analysis and final evidence reports are fully permitted.

nodes.label: Sanctioned Databricks Deployment Exception
nodes.rationale: The /subir-*-databricks and /app-* commands under .claude/commands/ are a manual, on-demand migration to a Databricks workspace. They upload only the data notebooks 01-06 and /report actually read, never modify report_pipeline.py, the 5 LLM roles, or local runtime dependencies, and all follow _contrato-despliegue-databricks.md. It is a standalone CLI-driven command tree, not an automation pipeline and not a reversal of the notebook-to-Python migration.

nodes.label: Retirement of the Lakeview AI/BI PoC
nodes.rationale: Lakeview runs neither Python nor arbitrary JS, so it could never show the notebooks' real analysis. The PoC (notebooks/databricks/, /deploy-databricks-dashboard) was retired and nothing in the repo creates Delta tables, views or dashboards any more.

nodes.label: LLM Safety and Quality Contract
nodes.rationale: Deterministic Python selects circuits, periods, series, critical points and attribution summaries; the LLM only interprets the structured context, must return schema-matching JSON, and must cite dates, critical_point_id, variables and summaries present in context. Chain-of-Thought via <think> blocks is encouraged before emitting final JSON. Save the exact prompt and context for every run; never log secrets or dump the raw dataset.

nodes.label: Missing Optional Columns Degradation Rule
nodes.rationale: The workflow must continue when optional columns are absent. Missing ones appear in metadata.unavailable_optional_columns and LLM output should mention the resulting data gaps without claiming those variables were observed.

nodes.label: Invalid LLM Output Quarantine
nodes.rationale: If LLM output does not validate, save the raw invalid output and validation errors under reports/reportescircuitos/artifacts/, print a clear message, and never present it as final analysis — a failed validation must be visible, not silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Required Local Validations (pytest + run_llm_eval)
nodes.rationale: Run `pytest -q` and `python evals/run_llm_eval.py` before considering changes complete; these stay local validations even though GitHub Actions handles Pages deployment.

nodes.label: Deterministic Coding Style Rules
nodes.rationale: Prefer pure functions under src/chec_local_interpreter; keep notebook cells short; treat identifiers as strings; parse FECHA with pd.to_datetime(errors='coerce'); coerce numeric analysis columns only in derived frames; keep optional columns optional and record unavailable ones in context metadata.
